name: African Lion
desc: Apex predator known for its majestic mane and social pride structure.
threats: Habitat loss, human-wildlife conflict, trophy hunting

name: Bengal Tiger
habitat: Tropical rainforests, mangroves, and tall grasslands
desc: Iconic solitary hunter with striking orange coat and dark black stripes.
conservation: Project Tiger reserves and habitat corridors
threats: Poaching for body parts, deforestation, prey reduction

name: African Bush Elephant
desc: The largest living terrestrial land mammal, possessing large fan ears and prehensile trunk.
conservation: Ivory trade bans and landscape corridors

name: Grizzly Bear
habitat: Woodlands, subalpine meadows, and river valleys
desc: Powerful bear with a distinctive shoulder hump and long digging claws.

name: Giant Panda
desc: Beloved black and white bear that feeds exclusively on bamboo shoots.
conservation: China bamboo corridor reserves & captive breeding

name: Cheetah
habitat: Dry forests, grasslands, and open plains
desc: The fastest land mammal on Earth, capable of accelerating from 0 to 60 mph in 3 seconds.
conservation: Cheetah Conservation Fund livestock guarding dogs
threats: Low genetic diversity, livestock farmer conflicts

name: Red Panda
desc: Tree-dwelling mammal with reddish-brown fur, ringed tail, and false thumb.

name: Snow Leopard
habitat: Steep rocky mountain ranges above tree line
desc: Elusive 'Ghost of the Mountains' equipped with thick fur and long tail for balance.
threats: Climate warming in alpine habitats, retaliatory killings

name: Gray Wolf
desc: Highly intelligent apex social pack predator with complex howl communication.

name: Red Kangaroo
desc: The largest marsupial in the world, traveling via high-speed bipedal hopping.

name: Giraffe
habitat: Arid savannas and open acacia woodlands
desc: The tallest living land animal, featuring a towering neck and dark prehensile tongue.

name: Hippopotamus
desc: Semi-aquatic megaherbivore known for its immense jaw gape and territorial aquatic pods.
threats: Ivory tooth trade, drought and river diversion

name: Mountain Gorilla
desc: Gentle giant primate led by a dominant silverback male in family troops.
threats: Snare poaching, human respiratory disease transmission

name: Platypus
desc: Egg-laying monotreme mammal with duck bill, beaver tail, and venomous ankle spurs.
threats: Dam construction, climate change drying rivers

name: Capybara
habitat: Dense vegetation adjacent to water bodies
desc: The largest rodent in the world, highly social and excellent swimmer.

name: Koala
desc: Arboreal marsupial that spends up to 20 hours a day sleeping in eucalyptus forks.

name: Meerkat
desc: Small mongoose known for standing upright on hind legs as sentinels.

name: Polar Bear
habitat: Arctic sea ice and coastal waters
desc: Largest living bear species, hyper-specialized for life on frozen sea ice.
conservation: Global climate action & sea ice monitoring
threats: Arctic sea ice loss due to warming

name: Plains Zebra
desc: Striped equid famous for massive annual migrations across the Serengeti.

name: Jaguar
desc: Largest feline in the Americas, with bite force capable of piercing turtle shells.

name: Blue Whale
desc: The largest animal ever known to have existed on Planet Earth.

name: Bald Eagle
desc: National emblem of the United States with white head feathers and massive 7-foot wingspan.

name: Emperor Penguin
habitat: Antarctic sea ice and pack ice
desc: Tallest penguin species, breeding during harsh sub-zero Antarctic winters.

name: Peregrine Falcon
habitat: Mountain cliffs, river valleys, and skyscrapers
desc: The fastest member of the animal kingdom, exceeding 200 mph in a hunting stoop dive.

name: Scarlet Macaw
desc: Large parrot adorned with bright red, yellow, and blue feathers.

name: Snowy Owl
habitat: Open arctic tundra and windswept coasts
desc: Striking white raptor adapted to freezing temperatures and 24-hour daylight hunting.

name: Flamingo (Greater Flamingo)
habitat: Saline mudflats, lagoons, and shallow lakes
desc: Wading bird famous for pink plumage derived from carotenoid pigments in its food.
conservation: Water level protection in salt lakes

name: Harpy Eagle
desc: Among the largest and most powerful eagles, equipped with 5-inch talons.

name: Peafowl (Indian Peafowl)
desc: Famous for the male peacock's iridescent blue crest and train of eye-spotted feathers.
conservation: National Bird protection status in India

name: California Condor
desc: Largest North American land bird, saved from extinction by captive breeding program.
threats: Lead poisoning from eating bullet fragments in carcasses

name: Hummingbird (Bee Hummingbird)
desc: The smallest bird in the world, flapping wings over 80 times per second.

name: Toucan (Keel-billed Toucan)
desc: Recognizable by its oversized rainbow-colored hollow bill used for thermoregulation.

name: Ostrich (Common Ostrich)
desc: The largest flightless bird, running at speeds up to 43 mph.

name: Great Horned Owl
desc: Nocturnal predator featuring prominent ear tufts and silent flight feathers.

name: Atlantic Puffin
habitat: Open ocean marine waters & sea cliffs
desc: 'Sea parrot' with colorful triangular beak that can carry over 10 small fish at once.
conservation: Nesting island rat eradication & sand eel fishery bans

name: Albatross (Wandering Albatross)
desc: Possesses the largest wingspan of any living bird (up to 11.5 feet), gliding for miles without flapping.

name: Shoebill Stork
desc: Prehistoric-looking bird with a massive shoe-shaped bill capable of decapitating fish.

name: Secretarybird
desc: Long-legged bird of prey that stomps venomous snakes with force 5 times its body weight.

name: Resplendent Quetzal
desc: Sacred bird of Maya mythology, with iridescent green plumage and 3-foot male tail streamers.

name: Hornbill (Rhinoceros Hornbill)
desc: Bird featuring a bright orange-red casque atop its bill, sealing females inside nest tree hollows.
threats: Palm oil deforestation, casque carving trade

name: Kiwi (North Island Brown Kiwi)
desc: Flightless nocturnal bird with hair-like feathers, nostrils at tip of beak, and large egg size.
threats: Predation by feral dogs and stoats

name: Cassowary (Southern Cassowary)
desc: Keystone rainforest seed disperser with a casque on head and dagger-like 5-inch toe claw.
threats: Vehicle strikes, dog attacks, habitat clearance

name: Green Iguana
desc: Large arboreal lizard with a row of spines along its spine and an impressive dewlap.

name: King Cobra
habitat: Dense highland forests and bamboo thickets
desc: The world's longest venomous snake, famous for expanding its neck hood when threatened.

name: Komodo Dragon
habitat: Dry open savannas and tropical forests
desc: The largest living lizard species on Earth, possessing serrated teeth and venomous bite.

name: Galapagos Giant Tortoise
desc: Long-lived tortoise species that can weigh over 500 lbs and live past 100 years.
threats: Invasive species eating eggs, historical overhunting

name: Saltwater Crocodile
desc: The largest living reptile, hypercarnivorous apex predator with supreme bite force.

name: Chameleon (Veiled Chameleon)
desc: Lizard capable of changing color, with independently mobile eyes and a long ballistic tongue.

name: Leatherback Sea Turtle
desc: The largest sea turtle, lacking a bony shell and covered instead by leather-like oily skin.
threats: Plastic pollution ingestion, egg poaching, net entanglement

name: Gila Monster
desc: Heavy, slow-moving venomous lizard with bead-like pink and black scales.

name: Green Anaconda
desc: The heaviest snake in the world, acquiring prey through aquatic constriction.

name: Bearded Dragon
desc: Popular Australian lizard known for its spiky throat beard used for defensive displays.

name: Rattlesnake (Western Diamondback)
habitat: Arid deserts, grassy plains, and canyons
desc: Venomous pit viper known for its warning tail rattle made of keratin segments.

name: Black Mamba
habitat: Savannas, rocky hills, and open woodlands
desc: Fastest land snake in the world, named for the ink-black coloration inside its mouth.

name: Frilled Dragon (Frilled Lizard)
desc: Lizard equipped with a large pleated neck frill that spreads out dramatically when frightened.
threats: Predation by feral cats, habitat burning

name: Thorny Devil
desc: Spiky desert lizard that collects water via microscopic grooves in its skin leading to its mouth.

name: Gecko (Tokay Gecko)
desc: Nocturnal arboreal gecko with specialized toe pads allowing it to walk effortlessly on glass and ceilings.

name: Hawksbill Turtle
desc: Sea turtle distinguished by a narrow beak and overlapping shell scutes once prized for tortoiseshell.
conservation: Tortoiseshell trade bans and reef protection

name: Nile Crocodile
desc: Aggressive freshwater crocodile known for ambush hunting zebra and wildebeest crossing rivers.

name: American Alligator
desc: Apex wetland predator with a wide rounded snout and dark armor-like scutes.

name: Marine Iguana
habitat: Rocky ocean shores and intertidal zones
desc: The only modern lizard with the ability to forage for food underwater in ocean currents.
threats: El Niño warming events, oil spills

name: Emerald Tree Boa
desc: Striking green arboreal snake that spends its entire life coiled over branches in rainforests.

name: Matamata Turtle
desc: Strange freshwater turtle with leaf-shaped camouflage head and neck used to suction up fish.

name: Poison Dart Frog
desc: Brilliantly colored frog that secretes potent neurotoxins derived from its wild insect diet.

name: Axolotl
desc: Paedomorphic salamander that retains its larval external gills throughout adult life.
conservation: Water quality recovery and breeding programs

name: Red-Eyed Tree Frog
region: Central America and northern South America
desc: Iconic green tree frog with large scarlet eyes and vibrant blue and yellow flanks.

name: American Bullfrog
habitat: Permanent freshwater bodies, ponds, and lakes
desc: Large vocal frog with deep bass calls that resemble a roaring bull.

name: Japanese Giant Salamander
desc: Second-largest salamander species in the world, growing over 4 feet long.

name: Fire Salamander
habitat: Deciduous forests with cool damp leaf litter
desc: Striking black salamander adorned with bright yellow warning blotches and skin toxins.

name: Goliath Frog
desc: The largest living frog on Earth, weighing up to 7 pounds and leaping over 10 feet.

name: Golden Toad
desc: Famous fluorescent orange toad species whose extinction became a symbol of climate change impact.

name: Cane Toad
habitat: Agricultural fields, urban areas, and open habitats
region: Central and South America (Invasive in Australia)
desc: Massive toad with large parotoid glands behind eyes that produce deadly bufotoxin.

name: Tiger Salamander
habitat: Deep burrows near ponds and woodlands
desc: Large terrestrial salamander with dark body covered in yellow vertical tiger stripes.

name: Glass Frog
habitat: Montane cloud forest vegetation over streams
desc: Translucent frog whose see-through abdominal skin reveals internal organs and beating heart.

name: Surinam Toad
habitat: Muddy forest river bottoms and swamps
desc: Flat star-fingered toad that embeds eggs into its back skin where toadlets hatch out directly.

name: Purple Frog (Pig-nosed Frog)
desc: Ancient living fossil frog with a rounded bloated body and pointed snout that lives underground year-round.

name: Hellbender Salamander
desc: Giant flat aquatic salamander with wrinkled skin folds used to absorb oxygen directly from water.
conservation: Stream restoration and artificial nesting boxes

name: Panamanian Golden Frog
habitat: Mountain stream banks in cloud forests
desc: National symbol of Panama that uses hand-waving 'semaphore' gestures to communicate above noisy streams.
conservation: Captive breeding and biosecure ark facilities

name: Marbled Newt
desc: Newt decorated with bright green and black marble patterns and a tall crest in breeding males.

name: Amazon Milk Frog
habitat: High canopy foliage near water hollows
desc: Arboreal frog with blue-gray skin and white bands that secretes a milky white defensive fluid.

name: Mudpuppy
desc: Fully aquatic salamander that retains bushy red external gills throughout its entire adult life.

name: Bumblebee Poison Frog
desc: Dart frog species featuring bold black and bright yellow bumblebee warning stripes.

name: Vietnamese Mossy Frog
habitat: Flooded caves and mossy mountain rock cliffs
desc: Master of camouflage with green and brown bumpy skin that perfectly mimics clumps of moss.

name: Black Spotted Newt
desc: Small colorful aquatic newt with olive skin and black spotted markings.

name: Clownfish
habitat: Sheltered coral reefs and sea anemones
desc: Bright orange reef fish famous for its immune mucus layer allowing symbiotic life in anemones.

name: Great White Shark
desc: Apex marine predator with powerful jaws containing up to 300 serrated teeth.

name: Whale Shark
desc: The largest non-mammalian vertebrate on Earth, docile filter feeder with white spot patterns.

name: Manta Ray
desc: Majestic oceanic ray with large triangular pectoral fins resembling underwater wings.

name: Lionfish
habitat: Coastal reef crevices and coral lagoons
desc: Striking venomous fish with fan-like pectoral fins and bold zebra warning stripes.

name: Regal Tang (Blue Tang)
desc: Vibrant blue reef fish made famous by the character 'Dory' in Finding Nemo.

name: Seahorse (Lined Seahorse)
habitat: Seagrass beds, mangroves, and coral reefs
desc: Unique fish where males carry and hatch fertilized eggs inside a brood pouch.

name: Hammerhead Shark
desc: Shark featuring a flattened hammer-shaped head ('cephalofoil') for 360-degree vision.

name: Red Piranha
habitat: Freshwater river basins and flooded forests
desc: Freshwater fish with razor-sharp interlocked teeth and strong jaw crushing force.

name: Electric Eel
desc: Knifefish capable of generating high-voltage electric shocks over 600 volts.

name: Angelfish (Freshwater)
desc: Popular aquarium fish with tall triangular fins and graceful swimming motion.

name: Ocean Sunfish (Mola Mola)
desc: The heaviest bony fish in the world, resembling a giant floating fish head.

name: Moray Eel (Green Moray)
habitat: Coral reef crevices and rocky caves
desc: Secretive eel with pharyngeal jaws inside its throat to pull prey into esophagus.

name: Sturgeon (Beluga Sturgeon)
desc: Ancient prehistoric fish prized for beluga caviar, living over 100 years.
threats: Poaching for caviar, river dam barriers

name: Pufferfish
desc: Defensive fish capable of inflating its body with water/air and harboring lethal tetrodotoxin.

name: Barracuda (Great Barracuda)
habitat: Nearshore coral reefs and open ocean
desc: Fast predatory ray-finned fish with prominent fang-like teeth and torpedo body shape.

name: Basking Shark
desc: The second-largest living shark species, swimming slowly with gaping mouth to filter plankton.

name: Betta Fish (Siamese Fighting Fish)
habitat: Shallow fresh water marshes and rice paddies
desc: Known for brilliant flowing fins and territorial male displays.
threats: Pollution, habitat loss in native range

name: Coelacanth
habitat: Deep ocean cave systems near volcanic islands
desc: Lobe-finned 'living fossil' fish once thought to have gone extinct 66 million years ago.

name: Flying Fish
habitat: Surface waters of open tropical oceans
desc: Fish equipped with large wing-like pectoral fins enabling glides over water surface up to 600 feet.

name: Swordfish
desc: Fast oceanic predator with a long flattened bill resembling a sword used to slash prey.

name: Monarch Butterfly
desc: Famous migratory butterfly with black, orange, and white lattice wing patterns.
lifespan: 2 - 6 weeks (up to 8 months for migratory generation)

name: Leafcutter Ant
habitat: Tropical rainforest floor and underground nests
desc: Eusocial insect capable of carrying leaf fragments 50 times its own body weight.

name: Honey Bee (Western Honey Bee)
habitat: Wild hollow trees, meadows, and hives
desc: Critical global pollinator living in structured colonies with queen, workers, and drones.

name: Praying Mantis (European Mantis)
desc: Predatory insect with folded front legs reminiscent of praying hands and a 360-degree head rotation.

name: Atlas Moth
diet: None as adult (Sustained by larval fat)
desc: One of the largest lepidopterans in the world with wing surface area over 60 sq inches.

name: Hercules Beetle
desc: Massive rhinoceros beetle with males featuring giant pincer-like horns longer than their body.

name: Green Darner Dragonfly
desc: Agile aerial predator capable of flying backwards, upside down, and hovering at 30 mph.

name: Seven-Spotted Ladybug
desc: Beneficial beetle with red wing covers and seven distinct black spots.

name: Goliath Beetle
desc: Among the heaviest insects on Earth, weighing up to 3.5 ounces in larval stage.

name: Firefly (Common Eastern Firefly)
habitat: Wetlands, agricultural fields, and wood edges
desc: Bioluminescent beetle producing cold light flash signals from abdominal lantern to attract mates.

name: Periodical Cicada (17-Year Cicada)
desc: Insect that spends 17 years underground before emerging synchronously in billions.

name: Luna Moth
desc: Luminous lime-green moth with long twisted hindwing tails designed to disorient bat sonar.

name: Stag Beetle
habitat: Oak woodlands and decaying wood piles
desc: Largest European beetle with males bearing oversized mandibles resembling deer antlers.

name: Rusty Patched Bumblebee
desc: Native wild bumblebee species distinguished by a rusty reddish patch on its abdomen.
threats: Pathogens from commercial hives, habitat loss

name: Orchid Mantis
desc: Master of aggressive mimicry with pink and white petal-shaped legs that attract unsuspecting bees.

name: Walking Stick (Giant Stick Insect)
desc: Cryptic insect that perfectly resembles a wooden twig, swaying in the wind to blend in.

name: Bullet Ant
desc: Ant notorious for possessing the most painful insect sting on Earth, comparable to a bullet wound.

name: Jewel Beetle
desc: Beetle celebrated for its iridescent metallic structural colors once used in jewelry.

name: Giant Water Bug (Toe-Biter)
desc: Large aquatic insect with raptorial front legs that injects digestive saliva into prey.

name: Blue Morpho Butterfly
habitat: Tropical rainforest lower canopy and ground
desc: Butterfly with iridescent electric blue upper wings caused by microscopic scale light diffraction.

name: Giant Weta
desc: Giant flightless cricket relative that is one of the heaviest insects in existence.
